title: Application Authentication
description: Implement JWT-based authentication in your applications with social login, OIDC, and SAML support.

data.text: When a user signs in through Cognito, they receive **JWT (JSON Web Token)** tokens. Your application validates these tokens to confirm the user's identity and permissions — without needing to call a database on every request.

data.title: Three Types of Tokens
items: **ID Token** — contains user profile claims (name, email, custom attributes)
**Access Token** — used to call APIs and confirm user authorization
**Refresh Token** — used to get new tokens without re-entering credentials

data.title: Validate a Cognito JWT in Python with PyJWT
data.content: This Python function validates the ID token from Cognito using the JWKS endpoint.
data.code:
import jwt
import requests
from jwt.algorithms import RSAAlgorithm

# Fetch the JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) from Cognito
JWKS_URL = 'https://cognito-idp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/us-east-1_abc123/.well-known/jwks.json'
jwks = requests.get(JWKS_URL).json()

# Build the public key from the JWK
key = RSAAlgorithm.from_jwk(jwks['keys'][0])

def validate_token(token: str) -> dict:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token,
            key,
            algorithms=['RS256'],
            audience='4kfeabc123',
            issuer='https://cognito-idp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/us-east-1_abc123'
        )
        return payload
    except jwt.ExpiredSignatureError:
        raise ValueError('Token has expired')
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError:
        raise ValueError('Invalid token')

data.text: Cognito supports federated login through **OIDC**, **SAML**, and social providers like **Google**, **Facebook**, and **Apple**. Users can sign in with an existing account, and Cognito links it to a user profile in your User Pool.

terms.definition: A compact, URL-safe token that represents claims between two parties.
OpenID Connect — an identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0.
Security Assertion Markup Language — an XML-based standard for exchanging authentication data.
JSON Web Key Set — a set of public keys used to verify JWTs.

data.title: Exercise: Validate a Token
data.description: Create a Lambda function that validates a Cognito ID token and returns the user's email and role. Use the Python code above as a starting point.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cognito issues JWT tokens after successful authentication
Validate tokens using the JWKS endpoint and your User Pool's public key
Social login and SAML/OIDC federation are built-in
